results.newText: US pet dogs and cats — what's the split?
results.reason: The original 'pet people' split cannot be sourced: APPA 2025 household data overlaps (53% of households own a dog, 39% own a cat, many own both), so no dog-vs-cat share of people exists. Reframed to the countable population: AVMA 2025 counts 87.3M pet dogs and 76.3M pet cats in the US, so dogs are 53% of all pet dogs+cats (87.3/163.6).
results.source: AVMA Pet Ownership and Demographics Sourcebook / Pet Owner Survey 2025: 87.3M dogs, 76.3M cats

results.reason: YouGov Daily Question, May 27 2022 (n=6,833 US adults): total/somewhat early bird 17%+19%=36%; somewhat/total night owl 28%+22%=50%; neither 8%, not sure 6%. Night owls are 50% of adults, not 58%. Chronotype science (MCTQ) puts most people in between, so the self-ID poll is the only honest two-way source.
results.source: YouGov, 'Are you more of an early bird or a night owl?', May 27 2022

results.newText: Where Americans actually live — how does the population split?
results.reason: The original 'dream home' preference cannot be a clean split: Gallup's 2018/2020 polls offer six choices (big city, small city, suburbs, town, rural), e.g. 2020: city 27%, town/rural 48%, suburbs 25%. Reframed to the hard demographic fact: 2020 Census, 80.0% of the US population lived in urban areas, 20.0% in rural areas.
results.source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census urban/rural classification (released Dec 29, 2022): 80.0% urban, 20.0% rural

results.reason: NCES Digest Table 306.10, fall 2023 degree-granting enrollment: 10,973,100 women vs 8,066,500 men out of 19,039,600 total = 57.6% women. Current 57 rounds down; the published figure rounds to 58.

results.reason: Parade/SheKnows 'What America Eats' survey (2013, ~4,000 US adults): 73% prefer a savory breakfast over sweet, so sweet = 27%. It is the only forced binary sweet-vs-savory breakfast poll found; newer polls (Happy Egg/OnePoll 2022) split answers across sweet/savory/mix and give no clean split. Caveat: the source is 2013 — flag for replacement if a newer forced-choice poll appears.
results.source: Parade / SheKnows, What America Eats survey, April 2013: 73% prefer savory breakfast

results.reason: Travel Channel / Open Mind Strategy Summer Travel Forecast 2019 (n=2,078 nationally representative): 63% said they would rather visit the beach than the mountains — a direct head-to-head. Current 64 is 1 point high. (Multi-choice polls like Ipsos 2025 give beach 41% vs mountains 11% among many options, not a split.)
results.source: Travel Channel / Open Mind Strategy, Summer Travel Forecast 2019: 63% beach over mountains

results.reason: REMOVE. Searched Pew Research Center Oct 2025 reading survey, Two Sides/Toluna and Guardian/Voxburner preference polls. Pew (the authoritative US source) measures overlapping usage — 64% read a print book, 31% an e-book, 26% audiobooks in the past year; many readers use both formats, so no print-vs-ebook 'split' exists. No published forced-choice US print-vs-ebook preference poll was found (the only forced-choice figures are UK youth or Irish/global lobby surveys). Any single number here would be invented.

CivicScience polling of US adults, Jan 2024-Jul 2025: forced choice coffee vs tea, 65% choose coffee, 35% tea. NCA past-day consumption (66% coffee vs 42-47% tea) overlaps because many drink both, so the forced-choice poll is the right source; current 74 is unsupportable.
results.source: CivicScience, Coffee or Tea polling, Jan 2024-Jul 2025: coffee 65%, tea 35%

results.newText: US paid workdays — how do they split?
results.reason: The original WFH-vs-office preference cannot be a clean split: Gallup (Nov 2025) has remote-capable workers preferring hybrid 61%, fully remote 33%, on-site 6% — hybrid dominates, so no two-way preference exists. Reframed to the measured behavior: Stanford's Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (WFH Research, June 2026 update) finds ~27% of all paid US workdays are worked from home, 73% in the office.
results.source: Barrero, Bloom & Davis, Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (WFH Research), June 2026: ~27% of paid workdays from home

results.reason: Heinz UK poll, June 2023 (13,000+ respondents): 63% store ketchup in the fridge, 37% in the cupboard. Current 72 is unsourced. Caveats: UK sample and a self-selected brand poll — the best published figure found; no US equivalent poll exists, so flag if US-only sourcing is required.
results.source: Heinz UK, 'Where do you keep yours?' poll, June 2023: 63% fridge, 37% cupboard

results.reason: Pew Research Center, 'Americans and Text Messaging' (survey Apr-May 2011, n=2,277): when asked how they prefer to be contacted, 31% of texters preferred texts, 53% preferred a voice call, 14% said it depends. The current 78 is the widely repeated marketing myth (conflating 'uses texting' with 'prefers texting'). Caveat: the rigorous forced-preference poll is 2011; no newer equivalent Pew preference question was found — YouGov Feb 2026 only asks whether messaging replaced calls (37% say most calls).
results.source: Pew Research Center, Americans and Text Messaging, Sept 2011: 31% prefer text, 53% prefer voice call
